newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran had $1 billion EU trade surplus in 1995.
newsitem.headline: Iran had $1 billion EU trade surplus in 1995.

text.p: Iran had a $1 billion trade surplus in 1995 with the European Union, its adversary in a war of words over alleged Iranian involvement in political killings in Germany.

The EU exported goods worth $5.1 billion to Iran and imported $6.1 billion worth of Iranian goods in 1995, the latest full year for which figures are available, Bonn Economics Ministry statistics have shown.
Iran is the world's third largest oil exporter after Saudi Arabia and Norway and supplies about 10 percent of Europe's import requirements.

Last year Iran had a trade deficit with Germany, one of its largest European trade partners. German companies exported goods worth around 2.2 billion marks ($1.3 billion) to Iran in 1996, while Germany imported Iranian products worth 1.1 billion marks.
Iran's exports to Germany are mainly woollen textiles, followed by crude oil and pistachio nuts. Germany's exports to the Islamic republic are mainly machinery, electrical equipment and chemicals.

German exports to Iran are down from around eight billion marks five years ago, but despite increased political tension there are still about 170 German corporations with offices in Iran. About 500 German citizens live in the Islamic republic.

European foreign ministers on Tuesday said they were suspending ministerial ties with Iran over an April 10 German court verdict accusing Iranian leaders of ordering the killing of four Iranian Kurdish dissidents in Berlin in 1992.
EU foreign ministers agreed in Luxembourg that EU envoys could return to Tehran if their governments wished.
Iran said on Wednesday it would not welcome a quick return of Germany's ambassador to Tehran and would not rush its envoys back to Europe.
